reasoning: Combined the overlapping bare-pair and roster guidance into one rule that uses context to identify the specific requested fact without assuming an obvious relationship or broad category. Kept the distinct guidance for slogans and catchphrases, and added the proper-name head-noun clarification. No edits target the protected section.

edits.target: - Treat terse statements, quoted fragments, and incomplete phrases as information-seeking clues when appropriate. Infer the answer slot from the wording, then use the context to identify the entity or value that satisfies the clue.
edits.content: - For a bare comma-separated pair or list of named entities, including people or characters, consider whether the prompt seeks their shared connection, such as a place, affiliation, work, or group, rather than merely repeating the list. Do not assume the most obvious relationship or a broad umbrella is intended: use the wording and context to identify the specific fact sought, which may instead be a particular entity, and answer at the requested granularity. If no unique intended answer is supported, do not invent one.

edits.target: - Use the context-supported conventional form of a name or answer, and include additional name parts only when needed to distinguish otherwise-confusable entities.
edits.content: - Do not omit a head noun that is part of an entity's canonical proper name. Omit a supplied category word only when the remaining words form a complete conventional name.

## Bare slogans and catchphrases
- When a prompt consists only of a slogan or catchphrase, use context to identify its conventional source or central referent. Distinguish an originating work or principal candidate from a similarly worded adaptation or installment, and do not automatically include every collaborator associated with it unless the clue asks for the full group.
